$comment: Per-service price ranges, related services and related posts, applied by scripts/migrate/content/fixes.mjs. Slugs only; the module resolves them to references and fails on any slug that is not a live document. Every price is a figure the live site publishes today, quoted in `source`. Rationale for every list is in README.md; the three services added by decision D18 carry their own `why`.

whole-home-rewiring.why: D18: the services its body links (panels, remodels, inspections) and troubleshooting; its cost guide first, then the aluminum and outdated-wiring posts and the two its signs and permit lines draw on.

hot-tub-pool-spa-electrical.why: D18: the services its body links (panels, surge protection, troubleshooting) and the outdoor page these posts hubbed on before; its cost guide and the pool pump post, then the panel-upgrade post that names hot tubs as a load.

whole-house-surge-protection.why: D18: the services its body links (panels, pool and spa, EV chargers) and troubleshooting; the two surge posts, then the posts that send readers to surge protection (monsoon, AC disconnect, mini-split).

priceRange.note: Standard 200-amp like-for-like panel replacement in the Phoenix metro. A full service replacement with a new all-in-one meter base and panel is typically $6,400–$8,750. Published on /faq and /services/panels, Oct 2026.
source: /faq, 'How much does an electrical panel replacement cost in Arizona?': "most electrical panel replacements fall between $5,200 and $6,500 for a standard 200-amp panel. If you need a full service replacement that includes a new all-in-one meter base and panel, that range is typically $6,400 to $8,750"
/services/panels body, 'What It Costs': "For a standard 200-amp like-for-like panel replacement in the Phoenix metro, expect $5,200 to $6,500 ... the range is typically $6,400 to $8,750"

priceRange.note: Typical installation of six recessed LED can lights in an existing (finished) ceiling, including fixtures, wiring, switches and labor. Published on /blog-posts/recessed-lighting-installation-phoenix and, from decision D16 (owner, 2026-10-19: the higher figure wherever the site disagreed; it said $1,050–$1,750), on /faq.
source: /blog-posts/recessed-lighting-installation-phoenix: "a kitchen with 6 recessed lights on a finished ceiling, wired to an existing circuit with a dimmer switch, typically lands between $1,400 and $2,200 all in"

/faq, 'How much does it cost to install recessed can lighting?', after D16-02 in migration/content-edits/decisions.json: "For a typical installation of six recessed LED can lights in an existing room, most homeowners in the Phoenix valley can expect to pay somewhere between $1,400 and $2,200."

priceRange.note: Level 2 (240-volt) charger at a home in the Phoenix area, depending on the distance from the panel and whether the panel has room for a new circuit; a panel upgrade adds to it. Published on /faq, Oct 2026.
source: /faq, 'How much does it cost to install an EV charger at home?': "Installing a Level 2 EV charger (240-volt) at a home in the Phoenix area typically costs between $750 and $3,500 depending on the distance from your panel to the charging location and whether your panel has room for a new circuit. If your panel needs an upgrade to support the charger, that adds to the cost."

notPriced.surge protection: /faq and both surge posts publish $400 to $800 installed for a whole-house surge protector (the /faq answer said $300 to $600 until decision D16, 2026-10-19), and since D18 there is a surge service document (/services/whole-house-surge-protection). It was added without a priceRange: service pages show no prices (owner rule), the figure stays on /faq and the two surge posts, and putting it in the service's structured data is left for the owner to approve. Left out.
notPriced.hourly rates: /faq quotes "$125 and $375 per hour" as what other Phoenix electricians charge, not a price of this business. Left out.
notPriced.electrical-upgrades: The /faq panel figures are for a home's 200-amp panel; electrical-upgrades is the commercial panel, feeder and service upgrade page. Left unpriced.
